question_text: Which one of the following statement is incorrect regarding the Charter Act of 1833?

options.a: Governor General in Council were given the power to legislate for the whole of the British territories in India.
options.b: Governor General of Bengal became the Governor General of India.
options.c: It added a law member to the Executive council of the Governor General, with voting power.
options.d: The monopoly of tea trade with China was abolished.

explanation: Option (a) is correct: By the Act of 1833, the Governor General in Council were given the power to legislate for the whole of the British territories in India. These laws were applicable to all persons, British or Indian foreigners or others and to the servants of the Company. They were enforceable by all courts in India. Option (b) is correct: The Governor General of Bengal became the Governor General of India. The Governor General in Council was to control, superintend and direct the civil and military affairs of the Company. Bombay, Bengal, Madras and other regions were subjected to the complete control of the Governor General in Council.

Other features of the Charter Act of 1833:  The Act made the Governor-General of Bengal as the Governor-General of India and vested in him all civil and military powers. Thus, the act created, for the first time, a government of India having authority over the entire territorial area possessed by the British in India. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.  The Act ended the activities of the East India Company as a commercial body, which became a purely administrative body. question_text: Consider the following statements: legislative councils to have non-official majority for the first time. bicameralism and direct elections in the country for the first time. merchants for the first time through the Charter Act of 1813. How many of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is also known as Morley-Minto Reforms (Lord Morley was the then Secretary of State for India and Lord Minto was the then Viceroy of India). It retained an official majority in the Central legislative council but allowed the provincial legislative councils to have a non-official majority. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Government of India Act of 1919 came into force in 1921. It introduced, for the first time, bicameralism and direct elections in the country. Thus, the Indian legislative council was replaced by a bicameral legislature consisting of an Upper House (Council of State) and a Lower House (Legislative Assembly). The majority of members of both the Houses were chosen by direct elections. Statement 3 is correct: Through the Charter Act of 1813, the Company was deprived of its monopoly of trade with India. It was allowed to continue with its monopoly of trade with China for the next 20 years. The Indian trade was thrown open to all British merchants.
